benefits.en: The weather may make or break the outdoor event.
benefits.zh: 你可以使用較短的方式，同時保留「可能成功，也可能失敗」的完整意思。

benefits.en: The expression shows that the listener should treat the situation seriously.
benefits.zh: 這個表達能提醒聽者認真處理相關情況。

benefits.titleEn: It Works Well with Modal Verbs
benefits.en: may make or break; might make or break; will make or break; will not make or break
benefits.zh: 這些情態動詞可以準確表達能力、可能性、預測或否定判斷。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful in Many Real Situations
benefits.en: jobs and interviews; businesses and customers; projects and teamwork; performances and competitions; friendships and trust; important choices and opportunities.
benefits.zh: 這個表達適用於工作、面試、生意、項目、比賽、人際關係及重要決定等多種情境。

benefits.en: Make or break means that the influence may be strong enough to determine success or failure.
benefits.zh: 只表示產生影響； make or break 則表示該影響可能足以決定成敗。

origin.statusEn: Gradual Development; Exact First Use Uncertain
origin.statusZh: 逐漸形成；確切首次用法不明

history.en: English had an older expression, make or mar, which communicated a similar contrast between success and ruin. Historical proverb records show that make or mar was used centuries before the modern wording. However, the exact process through which break replaced mar has not been firmly established, so the expression should not be connected to one dramatic invention story.
history.zh: 英語中較早已有 make or mar 這個表達，同樣用來對比成功與毀壞。 歷史諺語記錄顯示，make or mar 在現代說法出現前數百年已有人使用。 不過，break 如何取代 mar 的確切過程仍未能肯定， 因此不應把這個表達說成源自某一個戲劇性的事件。

history.en: The strong contrast naturally came to describe a person, action or decision capable of causing either success or failure. Merriam-Webster records the related hyphenated adjective make-or-break from 1919, although that date should not be treated as the invention date of every related use.
history.zh: 這種強烈對比逐漸用來形容足以令事情成功或失敗的人物、行動或決定。 Merriam-Webster 記錄了帶連字號的形容詞 make-or-break 在1919年的用法，但不應把該年份視為所有相關用法的創造年份。

origin.memoryEn: One important factor may build success—or destroy the chance of it.
origin.memoryZh: 一項重要因素可以成就成功，也可以摧毀成功的機會。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：使用 or，而不是 and
rules.en: The expression presents two opposite possible results: success or failure.
rules.zh: 這個表達指出兩個相反的可能結果：成功或失敗。

rules.titleEn: The Expression Normally Needs an Object
rules.titleZh: 規則二：這個表達通常需要受詞
rules.en: The interview may make or break.
rules.zh: 在本練習中，答案應清楚指出甚麼事情可能成功或失敗。

rules.titleEn: The Factor Must Be Truly Important
rules.titleZh: 規則三：相關因素必須真正重要
rules.en: The colour of his pen may make or break his application.
rules.zh: 除非原句清楚表示某項因素可能決定最終結果，否則不應使用這個慣用語。

rules.titleZh: 規則四：保留可能性及確定程度
rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a possibility into a more certain prediction.
rules.zh: 錯誤答案把「可能」改成較確定的預測。

rules.titleZh: 規則五：可以使用否定形式
rules.en: This means the mistake is not important enough to determine the final result.
rules.zh: 這表示該錯誤不足以決定最終結果。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use Hyphens in the Verb Expression
rules.titleZh: 規則六：動詞用法不使用連字號
rules.en: The adjective make-or-break is related, but it is not the target form practised in this exercise.
rules.zh: 形容詞 make-or-break 與本課表達有關，但並不是本練習要求使用的目標形式。

rules.en: The factory can make the glass or break it.
rules.zh: 這項決定可能會決定生意的成敗。 工廠可以製造玻璃，也可以把玻璃打破。

examples.en: The decision may make or break the business.
examples.zh: 這項決定可能會決定生意的成敗。

rules.en: The final interview may make or break the application.
rules.zh: 如果某項因素只有輕微影響，使用 affect、help 或 influence 會更加準確。

rules.titleZh: 規則九：目標字詞應連在一起

rules.titleEn: Use the Exact Target in This Exercise
rules.titleZh: 規則十：本練習必須使用指定目標
rules.zh: 真實英語中可能會出現其他相關形式，但本練習的每個答案都必須包含：
